A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Nested Subspace Networks work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the expanded title and reorganized appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 classification experiments, accuracy-versus-rank evaluations of adapted LLMs, and appendix analyses of learned weights and subspace containment.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification and LLM experiments and adds empirical energy-decay profiles and monotonicity-violation analyses.

M1.justification: The shared prefix-based low-rank architecture, SVD initialization and uncertainty-weighted anchor/variant objective in Equation 3 remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 and the expanded explanations document existing procedures rather than establish a revised method.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10 classification using ImageNet features and the existing LLM downstream evaluations remain the task coverage. The new energy-decay analyses inspect model weights rather than introduce another dataset or test scenario. Identifying ResNet-18 as the feature extractor supplies previously missing detail.

E2.justification: The direct comparison against FLOP-matched specialist dense MLPs in v1 Section 4.1/Figure 4 is removed, eliminating an important comparison supporting the specialist-matching claim. V2 adds dense-model controls for energy ordering in Section 4.2/Appendix C.5. Figure 2's native-rank-versus-truncation comparison and Table 1's comparator set remain; newly discussed methods such as MatFormer and Flextron are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a diagnostic protocol using rank-1024 factors, component norms, adjacent-index monotonicity checks and layer/depth aggregation. The FLOP-matched specialist evaluation is omitted, while retained accuracy experiments keep their reported settings. Newly specified preprocessing and regularizer implementation details do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices C.4–C.5 add a substantial investigation of the previously untested energy-decay assumption: component-energy profiles, layer-level violations, dense-model controls and depth-resolved comparisons. Existing objective ablations, interpolated-rank curves, subspace-containment tests and weight-similarity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new diagnostics report mean and standard deviation across layers and binomial standard errors for depth-resolved violation rates, notably Figure 14. Table 1's mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies explicit repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 does not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: V2 removes the specialist-comparison results in v1 Figure 4, including the rank-2 accuracies of 62.3% for Base MLP and 62.1% for NSN. It adds extensive energy-profile and violation results; Figure 13 reports 0.00% NSN versus 46.95% dense-model violations for that comparison. Table 1 and the retained LLM accuracy curves are unchanged, so this is a change in reported evidence rather than demonstrated performance improvement.

T1.justification: V2 adds a full-row-rank sufficient-condition lemma for nestedness, derivations of convexity and optimal uncertainty weights, the stationary relationship between log-variance and residual loss, and a training-cost analysis. These substantially expand the formal justification. The original interpolation bound and its proof are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution box and discussion retain the central claims of post-hoc adaptation, granular compute control, matching specialist models and approximately 50% FLOPs reduction for a five-percentage-point accuracy loss. The specialist-matching contribution remains despite removal of its direct comparison figure.

C2.justification: V2 interprets energy ordering as arising from NSN parameterization/training and sparse violations as optimization noise. It adds substantive explanations of loss-scale invariance, residual-loss tracking and tradeoffs with gradient-based weighting. Section 6 newly identifies the shared rank across layers as a limitation, while Section 3's takeaway explicitly conditions interpolation behavior on energy decay.

D1.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 newly specify frozen ResNet-18 features, 512-dimensional representations, 224-by-224 preprocessing, classifier placement, detached anchor logits and normalized hidden-feature regularization. Algorithms 1–4 document forward passes, training and log-variance initialization. A code/results link and reproducibility statement are also added; these are substantial disclosures, not evidence of changed experiments or independently verified code availability.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning against flag-manifold methods, MatFormer, Flextron, LLAMAFLEX, SortedNet, AdaLoRA, WeLore and adaptive-learning research. It develops distinctions between parameter-space rank hierarchies, representation-space nestedness and structural slicing/routing, going well beyond the earlier related-work discussion.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the motivation, substantially expands explanations of the architecture and objective, and reorganizes Section 4 around explicit questions. Appendices are restructured into related work, experimental details, additional analyses, theory and pseudocode. The title gains an LLM emphasis, and reproducibility, impact and acknowledgement statements are added.

P2.justification: The specialist-comparison Figure 4 is replaced by an energy-profile display, with further new diagnostic Figures 11–14, Table 4 and four algorithm blocks. Existing figures are substantially redistributed across the document; v1 Figure 11 survives as v2 Figure 15. Most retained plots and Tables 1 and 3 preserve their displays and values.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision and reproducibility through the explicit nestedness condition, loss derivations, implementation specifications, pseudocode and fuller treatment of closely related methods. The gain is limited by removing the direct FLOP-matched specialist comparison while retaining its associated contribution claim. Appendix C.4 also gives unreconciled violation summaries of 0.04% and about 1%, weakening the clarity of the new validation. These tradeoffs support a limited overall improvement.
